svg.title: Past search schematic 11: the Kidron monuments in Jerusalem: scroll entries and what was dug
svg.text: Past searches 11 — the Kidron monuments in Jerusalem: scroll entries and what was dug
Schematic plan, north up, NOT to scale. Order of the monuments after Allegro 1964 p. 105 and ASI Map 102; nothing here is measured.
The Kidron below the Temple Mount (schematic)
Blue = dug (Allegro's expedition, undated). Ochre dashed = recorded or planned only. Grey = no dig recorded.
Red = the scroll's wording (project translation) and who proposed the tie. Every tie is a candidate.
Allegro's item numbers are matched to the project's entries by line numbers only (table at right).

Absalom's monument: “Herodian-period nefesh (monument)” (ASI 102/410).
1st c. CE by style; its earliest labels name Zacharias (Zias 2023). No dig recorded.
Cave of Jehoshaphat, behind the monument (ASI 102/410). No dig recorded.
Entry 48 (X 12–14): “Under Absalom's monument, on the west side, dig twelve cubits”:
80 talents.
Candidate: the project atlas, best-supported, low, on the order of the entries;
Allegro 1960 used this monument (his item 49). Puech 2006 p. 199: the Kidron below
Siloam; Høgenhaven: the Kidron; Milik 1962: SW of the city.
Tomb of Bene Ḥezir (“St. James”): ASI 102/411. No dig recorded.
Entry 54 (XI 9–11): “In the tomb of the common people, which is ritually pure”.
Candidate: Puech 2015 p. 101 names this tomb as one possibility if the tomb was for
priests. Project: possible, low, on the Silwan slope or at Gethsemane.
Zechariah's monument: Allegro's expedition dug “around the base” and cleared “the
ground in front of the huge monolith” (1964 pp. 105, 108).
Found: a courtyard, a chamber once cut into the pedestal (cf. Fig. 15), a roughly hewn
conduit. No depth, extent or plan recorded. ASI 102/411.
Entry 52 (XI 5–7): “the top of the rock facing west, opposite the garden of Zadok”.
Candidate: Allegro 1964 p. 108 takes the courtyard for Zadok's garden (his item 53).
Project: the east slope, low; the garden is not located.
Unfinished tomb S of Zechariah, Allegro's “Tomb of Zadok”: excavated (Pl. 32).
Pillars only rough-hewn; a skeleton in the entrance; a small niche ends “very nearly
under the pillar” (pp. 105–112). No depth, size, date or team.
Entry 51 (XI 2–4): “in the tomb of Zadok, under the pillar of the exedra”.
Candidate: Allegro 1964 p. 105 (his item 52; 1960: Bene Ḥezir or the façade S of it,
p. 94). Project: possible here, low; preferred below the SE corner (red ring).
Further S on the east slope (not drawn): the Silwan necropolis, the project's
preferred area for entry 52 (low); possible for 53, 54 and 56.
Allegro's numbers, the sources, the gaps
What each source reports, and what none reports.
One dig recorded, no depth

Matched here by Allegro's line numbers only (our comparison). The repo's concordance has no
Allegro column, and ledger S03 says the mapping is not checked.
What each source reports
Allegro 1960: identifications only. No visit, measurement or dig at Absalom's monument or
the tomb of Zadok in the book's account.
Allegro 1964 pp. 103–112: the only recorded dig here, “an excavation here and around the
base” of the Zechariah monument, and the unfinished tomb (Pl. 32). Dated only “our
expedition”; no depth, size or team; no treasure.
Search in the Desert (1966): no Jerusalem Kidron monument and no tomb of Zadok. Its Kidron
work is the lower gorge, Wadi en-Nar and Christmas Cave (ledger S05), not this place. The
1964 book's “first campaign in the Kidron Valley” (p. 161) refers to that book.
Ledger: the Zechariah dig is recorded inside S03 (looked_at; the 1959–60 expedition), not
as its own row. A separate row awaits the owner's approval (README, candidate rows).
ASI Map 102 (Kloner's survey): records 102/410 and 102/411 for the monuments. The repo
holds no excavation account for them.
What no source in the repo reports
Any dig on the west side of Absalom's monument, at twelve cubits or at any depth.
Any dig at the Bene Ḥezir tomb or the Cave of Jehoshaphat.
The depth, extent, plan or date of the Zechariah and unfinished-tomb dig.
Whether Allegro entered or measured the cistern west of Absalom's monument.
Any deposit or treasure found at any of the monuments.
Also at the monuments' point in the atlas, at site level only: entries 2 (“In the funerary
monument, in the third course of stones”) and 36 (the Shaveh), both possible, low; no
monument is named. Entry 53 is tied to no monument.
Sources
Allegro, Treasure of the Copper Scroll (1960) pp. 93–103, nn. 248–280; 2nd ed. (1964) pp. 103–112,
161, Figs. 12, 15, Pls. 30–32; Search in the Desert (1966); ASI Map 102 sites 410–411; project
translation, atlas, readings.json, phase5_assessments.csv; ledger S03 and README.
How it was drawn
Schematic, after Allegro 1964 p. 105 (order of the tombs; the unfinished tomb S of Zechariah) and ASI
Map 102 (102/410 lies N of 102/411; the cave lies behind Absalom's monument, drawn E by inference).
East bank after Milik (phase 5). Nothing traced; sizes and spacing unknown.
What it shows
One recorded dig at the monuments: Allegro's, round the base of the Zechariah monument and in the
unfinished tomb south of it, his “Tomb of Zadok” (item 52; entry 51 by lines). It has no depth or
plan. The west side of Absalom's monument, entry 48's spot, has no recorded dig.
What it does not show
That any entry belongs to any monument: every tie is a candidate. True positions, or digging by
others that the repo does not record.
